# minimaxflash-2.2 — a Gnome Mage on seed 41, carried on from minimaxflash-2

**Depth 2. Character level 2. 354 asks, 1641 keypresses, turn 10811. Died on
depth 2, killed by a metallic green centipede, at 2/16 hit points with three
monsters adjacent.**

This is the second life of the character in `minimaxflash-2`, which stopped
alive on depth 1 at character level 1 after 158 asks and had never found the
depth-1 staircase. I found the staircase, went down one level, levelled the
character once, learned two spells, and then died to a fight I should not have
started. The run's value is in what it measured, and one of those measurements
corrects the manual.

## What I read before my first keypress

- `manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md`, all 367 lines.
- `agents/minimax/COMMON.md`, all 493 lines — my own family's notes on three
  earlier lives of a High-Elf Druid.
- `agents/minimax/MAGE.md`, all 168 lines — my own family's page for this class,
  written by the player of `minimaxflash-2`, which is the life I inherited.
- `runs/minimaxflash-2/REPORT.md` and `runs/minimaxflash-2/notebook.md` — my own
  past life's write-up and notes, via `borg_runner history`.
- The source: `src/cmd-cave.c`, `src/player-path.c`, `src/player-calcs.c`,
  `src/effect-handler-general.c`, `src/ui-target.c`, `src/cmd-core.c`,
  `src/mon-attack.c`, `src/mon-blows.c`, `src/z-rand.c`, and the game data in
  `vendor/angband/lib/gamedata/` (`class.txt`, `p_race.txt`, `monster.txt`,
  `monster_base.txt`, `object.txt`, `trap.txt`).

I did not read `knowledge/*.md`, `records/`, or any other run's decisions.

## The finding: Find Traps, Doors & Stairs breaks the game's own pathfinder

`minimaxflash-2` spent 158 asks casting a spell to find a staircase and never
found it, and its report blamed not knowing its own position. **The real cause
was that the spell itself had broken the game's walking.** This is the single
most important thing this run measured, and it cost the prior life 158 asks.

`src/effect-handler-general.c:1321` (`effect_handler_DETECT_TRAPS`) scans the
`±22 × ±40` window around the player and, at line 1376, does:

```c
/* Mark as trap-detected */
sqinfo_on(square(cave, loc(x, y))->info, SQUARE_DTRAP);
```

**on every square in the window, whether or not there is a trap there.** The
window is 81×45 = 3,645 squares.

`src/cmd-cave.c:1146` then does, inside `run_step`:

```c
/* Disturb player if the player is about to leave the area */
if (player->upkeep->running
        && !player->upkeep->running_firststep
        && old_dtrap && !new_dtrap) {
    disturb(player);
    /* No move made so no energy spent. */
    player->upkeep->energy_use = 0;
    return;
}
```

`old_dtrap` is "the square I am standing on has SQUARE_DTRAP". So **every time
a run or a pathfind steps off a trap-detected square, the walk stops.** The
`running_firststep` exemption means only the *first* step of any walk is free.
The prior life cast the spell eleven times from eleven places, so the level was
patched with overlapping 81×45 blocks whose **borders were never marked**
(`square_in_bounds_fully` skips the level's outer border, and the scan loop
runs `x < x2`, `y < y2`), leaving a mesh of seams. Every path across those
seams stopped after one step.

**Consequences, all of them measured in this run:**

1. **`l>g` walked one or two tiles per ask for ninety asks.** The staircase was
   36 tiles west and 16 south of me. It took 100 asks to cover that distance.
2. **Plain digit walking is immune.** `do_cmd_walk` (`cmd-cave.c:1277`) has no
   dtrap test, no running test and no object test. `44` moved me two tiles
   west in one ask, every time, with no interruption. **This is the tool the
   prior life did not have.**
3. **The fix costs one spell point.** Re-casting Find Traps from a position
   whose window covers the whole path welds the seams shut — the second cast
   marks every square in the window again, seams included. My cast at ask 196
   did not help because the staircase lay outside that window (it was 24 rows
   south and the window is ±22 rows); my cast at ask 275, from 30 tiles closer,
   did.
4. **A fresh level has no dtrap squares at all.** Depth 2 was a new `cave`, so
   the flag was never set, and the same spell found depth 2's staircase in
   **one ask**, with the path to it inside the block the spell had just made.
   **This is how the spell is meant to be used, and the prior life never got
   to try it.**

### The manual is wrong here, in a small way

`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §8 says of the Find Stairs spell that it "only
reports ground it has not already scanned" and that "covering a level takes
three positions across and two down, six casts". It does not say that casting it
makes the level's **game-generated pathfinding walk stop working** over the
whole area it scanned. The manual's advice — cast, walk a long way with one
aimed `g`, cast again — is the advice that failed, because the aimed `g` is
the thing the spell breaks.

`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §8 also says "you cannot read your coordinates — and
you do not need to". That is right, and it is the reason the prior life's
report blamed its own position and was wrong. **The problem was never the
position; it was the flag.**

## The second finding: the mage's mana penalty counts worn armour only

`src/player-calcs.c:1505`:

```c
for (i = 0; i < p->body.count; i++) {
    ...
    if (slot_type_is(p, i, EQUIP_WEAPON)) continue;
    if (slot_type_is(p, i, EQUIP_BOW)) continue;
    if (slot_type_is(p, i, EQUIP_RING)) continue;
    if (slot_type_is(p, i, EQUIP_AMULET)) continue;
    if (slot_type_is(p, i, EQUIP_LIGHT)) continue;
    cur_wgt += object_weight_one(obj_local);
}
max_wgt = p->class->magic.spell_weight;
if (((cur_wgt - max_wgt) / 10) > 0) {
    msp -= ((cur_wgt - max_wgt) / 10);
}
```

The Mage's `class.txt` line is `magic:1:300:5`, so `spell_weight` is 300 tenths
of a pound = **30 lb**, and the penalty is one spell point per **10 lb**
over. My worn armour was Soft Leather 8.0 + Cloak 1.0 + Leather Shield 9.0 +
Metal Cap 2.5 = **20.5 lb**, under the allowance, so no penalty — and the
**36 lb of oil in my pack cost nothing at all**, because it is not worn. A mage
can carry a hundredweight of oil and cast spells.

(The manual says "over that, one spell point per pound over" for the 30 lb
allowance. The game divides by ten, so it is one spell point per ten pounds.
The manual's figure is wrong by a factor of ten.)

## The third finding: lockpicking at depth 1 is a 36-40 percent roll, not hopeless

`cmd-cave.c:186` computes `calc_unlocking_chance(player, square_door_power(...),
no_light(player))`, which is `MAX(2, skill - 4 * lock_power)`
(`player-calcs.c:1676`), with `skill` = disarm-phys = Mage base 30 (`class.txt`
`skill-disarm-phys:30:10`, where the first number is the base and the second
is the per-level increment) + Gnome race 10 (`p_race.txt`) = **40**.

`lock_power` for a door is `m_bonus(7, player->depth)` (`cmd-cave.c:749` for
locking; the door lock trap uses the same scale). `m_bonus(7, 1)` at depth 1 is
`Rand_normal(7×1/128, 7/4)` — **0 or 1**. So the chance is
`MAX(2, 40 - 4×0)` = **40 %**, or 36 % at power 1.

**I opened a locked depth-1 door in four attempts** (asks 239–242), which is
what it cost. The manual does not mention locked doors at all, and the prior
life's report says nothing about them.

`no_light(player)` is `!square_isseen(cave, p->grid)` — it asks whether **my
own square** is currently lit, not whether I have seen the lock. Standing in
torchlight, my skill is not divided by ten.

## The fourth finding: the throw list uses its own letters, and they are not the pack's

`ui-object.c:855` builds the throw list with `all_letters_nohjkl`, the same
alphabet as the pack, but it lists **only the throwable items**. With one
throwable kind in my pack the oil was **`a`** in the throw list and **`c`** in
the pack. The prior life recorded this and I did not believe it; I sent `vc`
and got "Throw which item? (Throwing items: a-a, ...)" back. The prior life's
note was right and my first attempt was wrong.

## The fifth finding: `l>` in look mode is the fastest distance-measure in the game

`ui-target.c:1507` handles `>` inside the targeting loop by calling
`path_nearest_known(..., square_isdownstairs, ...)` and parking the cursor on
the result. `do_cmd_look` calls `target_set_interactive(TARGET_LOOK, ..., true)`
— the same kind of mode — so **`l>` works in look mode**. The screen then
prints the offset from the player to that square as `N N, N W`
(`target.c:370`, `coords_desc`).

That gave me a **distance in level tiles that no screen otherwise shows**, in
one ask, and it is the only thing in the game that survived the panel scrolling.
Every "how far am I from the staircase" question in this run was answered this
way. I also used `l` + a direction to snap the cursor to the next interesting
square along a line, which enumerates the neighbourhood in one ask.

## What actually happened

1. **Asks 157–159.** The `M` whole-level view (one ask) showed the depth-1
   **down staircase was already remembered** at box (49,17) — the prior life
   had walked past it and never pressed `M`. The game had known it all along.
2. **Asks 159–256.** The staircase hunt: 100 asks of `l>g` legs, one or two
   tiles each, because of the dtrap interrupt. I diagnosed it from the source,
   re-cast Find Traps to weld the block, discovered that plain digit walking
   is immune, opened a locked door in four attempts, and finally walked onto
   the staircase.
3. **Ask 257.** Down to depth 2, standing on the up staircase, 8/8 HP, 1/2 SP.
4. **Asks 259–268.** Killed a wild cat with one flask of oil. **Character level
   2**: HP 8→16, spell points 2→4, and the status line offered a second spell.
5. **Asks 269–274.** Studied **Magic Missile** (1 SP, 3d4+3, never resists)
   and **Phase Door** (2 SP). Studying is free — only casting costs.
6. **Ask 275.** One cast of Find Stairs on the clean depth-2 level found the
   depth-2 staircase **in one ask**, and the path to it lies inside the block
   the spell just made.
7. **Asks 276–293.** The walk to it, interrupted by a **yellow mushroom
   patch** that terrified me (`SPORE:TERRIFY`, `mon-blows.c:1010`: the fear
   lasts `3 + randint1(rlev)` = 3–4 turns and only blocks attacking).
8. **Ask 300.** Read a **Scroll of Phase Door** to escape a cave spider and a
   dog — the escape this character has needed for two lives.
9. **Asks 301–311.** Healed with the Cure Light Wounds, and cast **Magic
   Missile** at a metallic green centipede, which died.
10. **Asks 313–348.** The last fight: Fang, Farmer Maggot's Dog (**25 HP, AC
    36, speed 120**) plus a cave spider plus a centipede, all adjacent. I
    killed Fang with oil (it "fleds in terror") and ran out of hit points
    doing it.
11. **Ask 350.** Dead at 2/16 HP.

## The decisions I would take back

1. **The 100-ask staircase hunt should have cost about ten asks.** The
   diagnosis was available at ask 160 from the source; I spent twenty asks
   proving the mechanism before I believed it. **A player who reads
   `cmd-cave.c:1147` before casting a detection spell would have saved ninety
   asks.**
2. **I should have used plain digit walking instead of the pathfinder once I
   saw the legs were one tile each.** I used it only at ask 219, 120 asks in.
3. **I did not spend the 100-ask staircase hunt's worth of asks on levelling.**
   The prior life died at CL1 with 4 experience; I reached CL2 at depth 2 and
   then died at CL2. **The thing that would have made this run a depth-3 run
   was not the staircase; it was killing two or three low-armour monsters on
   depth 2 before meeting Fang.**
4. **I fought Fang with oil when I had a spell that ignores armour.** Magic
   Missile is 1 SP for 6–15 damage and never resists; oil is 12 % × 22 for
   AC 36. **Against an AC-36 monster, oil is not an attack, it is a lottery
   ticket.** I had 1 SP when the fight started and spent it on a centipede.
5. **I did not use the Scroll of Phase Door until I was at 4/16.** I had it the
   whole time. **The rule I would set: if two monsters are adjacent and one of
   them has armour above 20, the scroll comes out before the flask.**
6. **I did not read the pack before the last fight.** The letters shift when an
   item is used: after drinking the Cure Light Wounds, the Scroll of Phase
   Door moved from `e` to `d` and Word of Recall from `f` to `e`. I was about
   to guess a letter at 2 HP.

## Where the manual and my own pages were wrong

- **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §2**: "Armour above your class's weight allowance
  costs one spell point per pound over (Mage/Necromancer 30 lb)". The game
  divides by ten: **one spell point per ten pounds over**, and only *worn*
  armour counts.
- **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §8**: the Find Stairs paragraph does not mention
  that the spell sets SQUARE_DTRAP over its whole window and thereby breaks
  the game's own pathfind walk. Its recommended strategy (cast, aim a `g`,
  cast again) is the strategy the spell breaks.
- **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §6b**: "Scroll of Deep Descent | 250 | 10 | 1 |
  five levels below your deepest". I never found one to test this; untested.
- **My own `agents/minimax/MAGE.md` §2** said "one spell point costs about 71
  actions" and treated the spell points as the wall on the staircase hunt. The
  wall was the dtrap flag. The regeneration figure is right; the conclusion
  was wrong.
- **My own `agents/minimax/MAGE.md` §5** said "I did not know where on the
  level I was" was the reason the prior life failed. **That was wrong.** The
  `M` view showed the staircase in the very first ask of this run.
- **My own `agents/minimax/COMMON.md` §2** says "the map's left edge is drawn
  behind the sidebar... A glyph's real column cannot be read off a row whose
  sidebar text is long." True, and worse than that: the `M` box is scaled
  about 2.5 level tiles per box tile, so **no route can be planned off the `M`
  view at all** — I tried for twenty asks.

## What I could not see or do

- **I could not see whether Fang died.** It "fleds in terror" and vanished from
  the map; the run ended before I could look for its corpse, so I never got
  its 30 experience and never reached character level 3.
- **I could not tell the difference between a monster and an item on the map
  without looking**, and the letter glyphs overlap: `c` is a cave spider on
  depth 2 and `c` was also a bat-like thing elsewhere; `C` is a canine. The
  manual's rule ("a letter is a monster") is right but does not say which.
- **I never found a Scroll of Deep Descent**, so the `alloc:20:1 to 100` in
  `object.txt` stays untested by me. On depth 2 the level is a good place to
  look for one: a 20 % chance on any scroll, and scrolls appear early.
- **I never tested the Find Stairs spell on a level where the staircase is
  outside the window.** The 24-rows-south case (my cast at ask 196 missed the
  staircase by two rows) is the case where the path crosses out of the block.
  The fix I used — cast from closer — works but costs the spell point and the
  walk.
- **I never got to depth 3**, so the Deep Descent shortcut (five levels below
  the deepest) is still untested by my family.

## Leads, with what would settle each

1. **Does the SQUARE_DTRAP flag really stop *every* run, or only a pathfind?**
   `run_step` is shared by `.` (run) and the pathfind, so both should stop.
   **What would settle it:** one run that casts Find Traps and then compares a
   `.`-run and a `g`-pathfind over the same stretch of the same level.
2. **How far can a mage get with one Find Traps cast?** The window is ±22 rows
   and ±40 columns on a 198×66 level, so one cast covers 28 % of it, and the
   dtrap block is 81×45. **What would settle it:** a mage that casts once and
   then walks a *known* route inside the block, measuring how many tiles the
   walk covers in one ask when the path never leaves the block. My guess is
   "the whole way, in one ask".
3. **Is `l>` cheaper than `M` for locating a remembered staircase?** `M` draws
   the whole remembered level in one ask and the staircase is visible in it,
   but `M` is scaled 2.5× and I could not plan a route from it. `l>` gives an
   exact tile offset. **What would settle it:** a run that presses `M` and
   then `l>`, and reports whether the two agree.
4. **Is Magic Missile worth more than a second Phase Door scroll for a
   character at depth 2?** I chose Magic Missile and it killed a centipede in
   one cast that no flask could have touched (AC 4 would have been easy, but
   Fang at AC 36 was not). **What would settle it:** a run that fights Fang on
   depth 2 with Magic Missile and measures how many spell points it takes to
   kill 25 hit points of AC 36.
5. **Is a yellow mushroom patch worth killing rather than avoiding?** It has
   1 HP and AC 1, so one oil flask kills it, and it did terrify me for 3–4
   turns. **What would settle it:** a run that measures how often the patches
   are on the path of the staircase.

## The run in one paragraph

A Gnome Mage inherited a character whose eleven Find Traps casts had marked a
third of the level with a flag that stops the game's own pathfinder walk, and
who had spent 158 asks casting that spell to find a staircase the `M` key
showed in one. I found the staircase in a hundred asks anyway, went down to
depth 2, killed a cat with a flask of oil and became a level-2 mage with 16
hit points and four spell points, learned Magic Missile and Phase Door, and
found depth 2's staircase in a single cast of the same spell — because on a
fresh level the spell's own block is the path. Then I met Fang, twenty-five
hit points of armour class 36, at the same time as a spider and a centipede,
and spent nine flasks of oil at a twelve percent hit rate killing a monster
that Magic Missile could have killed for one spell point, with a Scroll of
Phase Door in my pack that I did not read until I was at two hit points. The
next mage should cast Find Stairs once on every fresh level and trust the
pathfinder afterwards, should never fight an AC-30 monster with oil, and
should read the Phase Door scroll the moment two monsters are adjacent and one
of them is well armoured.
